lines: Well, hello there, neighbour! You must be {player}, the new one on the green. I'm Mr. Palmer.
I look after things round here. The town meetings, the gazebo lights, the pumpkins that roll off Poppy's cart.
{player}: Nina said you know everything about this town.
(Mr. Palmer chuckles and checks his pocket watch.) Everything? No, no. Nearly everything. The old oak keeps a secret or two.
Now, a few tips for a new neighbour. Press {interact} to talk to anyone. People do different things at different times of day, so try again later if someone's busy.
{player_menu} opens your menu: your quests, the map, your bag. {map} goes straight to the map, and the star on it shows where to go next.
And if you're ever tired, your bed will let you sleep the hours away.
Off you go and say hello to a few more folks. Theo and Mr. Page are on the bench, and Dottie and Ozzie are about the green. They'll be glad to meet you.
Met a few of the neighbours? Good, good. Everyone's a little bit odd here, and that's what makes it home.
(He glances at the oak.) Midnight comes round quicker than you'd think.
Still up, {player}? (He looks at the oak, then at his watch, then at you.) Hm. Of course you are.
Whatever you find at midnight, be kind to it. And be kind to yourself. Everyone's new somewhere.
Well, hello there, neighbour! I'm Mr. Palmer. I look after things round here. Town meetings, the gazebo, that sort of thing.
{player}: Mr. Palmer?! You look just like the mayor of Galaxity!
(Mr. Palmer looks left. Then right. Then he leans down and whispers.)
Shh! Nobody here knows about that. On this side of the portal I'm just plain old Mr. Palmer.
Lots of us have a Galaxity side, you know. You look a bit different over there yourself, I expect.
{player}: I do?
Everyone does! That's the fun of it.
Ahem! Friends, neighbours, and anyone who's had too much kettle corn! In a moment, we let our lanterns go.
May they carry our wishes up... and wherever else they might be going. (He glances at the old oak.)
A tremor? Oh, that. The old pipes under the green. Yes. Pipes. Very old pipes.
(He checks his pocket watch. Then the old oak. Then his watch again.)
Off you pop, {player}. Nothing to worry about. Nothing at all.
Hm? You saw an envelope on my porch? Oh! That's from my... pen pal. Lives very far away. Terrible handwriting. Lovely person.
(He tucks something lilac into his coat pocket, very quickly.)
Galaxity? Ha! Did it say Galaxity? It must have said... Galveston. Yes. Galveston. Well! Lovely weather for it.
Ah, the Autumn Festival! Every year since I was a boy. And every year, the hayride goes round exactly once more than anyone expects.
Have you tried bobbing for apples? Hank keeps the best ones for the third go.
(Mr. Palmer jumps.) Oh! Goodness! {player}! Just... admiring the old oak. Lovely tree. Lovely bark.
{player}: At midnight?
Best time for it! It hums a bit this time of night, doesn't it? (He winks.) Off you go, then. And mind you're home by one.
Morning, neighbour! Tea on the porch. Best way to start the day. Well, second best. The first is not losing the string lights.
Lunch at the diner. Gus pretends he doesn't save me the window seat. He saves me the window seat.
Town business! Today: should the gazebo be painted white, or a slightly different white? Very important.
Oh dear, oh dear. The autumn festival's coming, and I've lost the string lights for the gazebo!
Three boxes of them. I put them down somewhere on my way round the green... by the diner? The bookshop? The inn?
Would you? You're a star. Just like back home, eh?
No rush. You live just round the corner, after all.
No rush. The festival can wait. The gazebo's very patient.
Any luck with those lights? By the diner, the bookshop or the inn, I'm sure of it. Fairly sure. A bit sure.
{player}: Mr. Palmer! I found all three boxes!
You found them! Splendid! Let's get them up.
(Mr. Palmer strings the lights round the gazebo roof. {player} holds the ladder. Click!)
(The gazebo glows warm and golden. A few people on the green stop to say ooh.)
There. Now it's a proper autumn evening.
Come by tomorrow and you can help with the festival. There's apple pie and hot apple juice.

rotate: Doesn't the gazebo look lovely? I keep walking past it just to look.
Off through the portal again tonight? Say hello to my other side for me.
Lovely evening for it. Autumn's my favourite. Everything smells like leaves.
The portal by the old oak opens at midnight. But you didn't hear that from me.
